title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 62 (Further issue of share capital)

content.overview: Section 62 governs further issue of share capital by a company having a share capital. Where the company proposes to increase its subscribed capital by the issue of further shares, such shares shall be offered (a) to existing equity shareholders pro rata to paid-up share capital by letter of offer (notice period not less than fifteen days or such lesser number of days as may be prescribed, and not exceeding thirty days; renunciation unless articles otherwise provide; after decline or expiry the Board may dispose of the shares in a manner not disadvantageous to shareholders and the company); or (b) to employees under an employees’ stock option scheme subject to special resolution and prescribed conditions; or (c) to any persons if authorised by special resolution, for cash or other consideration, if the price is determined by the valuation report of a registered valuer subject to Chapter III and prescribed conditions. Notice under (1)(a)(i) shall be despatched through registered post, speed post or electronic mode to existing shareholders at least three days before the opening of the issue. Sub-sections (3)–(6) address conversion of loans or debentures into shares where terms were approved by special resolution before issue, and Government-directed conversion.
content.glance: Default rights offer pro rata (15 days or lesser prescribed–30 days; renunciation; Board disposal); ESOP (special resolution); preferential (special resolution + registered valuer); 3-day notice dispatch; conversion and Government-directed routes.
content.study:
Section 62 is the principal further-issue provision.

Statutory test
1. Trigger: company having a share capital proposes to increase subscribed capital by issue of further shares.
2. Rights route — section 62(1)(a): offer to equity holders at the date of the offer in proportion, as nearly as circumstances admit, to paid-up share capital on those shares, by letter of offer. Conditions: (i) notice specifying number offered and time not less than fifteen days or such lesser number of days as may be prescribed and not exceeding thirty days; (ii) unless articles otherwise provide, offer includes right of renunciation and notice must state that right; (iii) after decline or expiry of time, Board may dispose of the shares in such manner as it thinks most beneficial to the company (not disadvantageous to shareholders and the company).
3. Notice dispatch — section 62(2): notice under (1)(a)(i) despatched by registered post, speed post or electronic mode to all existing shareholders at least three days before the opening of the issue.
4. ESOP route — section 62(1)(b): to employees under a scheme of employees’ stock option, subject to special resolution and prescribed conditions.
5. Preferential route — section 62(1)(c): to any persons if authorised by special resolution, whether or not including persons in (a) or (b), for cash or consideration other than cash, if price determined by valuation report of a registered valuer, subject to Chapter III and prescribed conditions.
6. Conversion — section 62(3): where any debentures or loan or any part thereof has been converted into shares under terms approved by special resolution before issue of debentures or raising of loan, the company shall file a prescribed return.
7. Government-directed conversion — section 62(4)–(6): Central Government may direct conversion of debentures or loan into shares in the circumstances and subject to the procedure stated (including appeal to Tribunal).

Boundary
Section 62 further-issue routes are distinct from section 42 private placement. A preferential issue under section 62(1)(c) may also engage section 42 and Chapter III public-offer rules depending on the facts. Section 23 identifies the high-level issue modes.

sections.heading: Rights issue — default route
sections.body: Further shares are offered to existing equity holders pro rata to paid-up capital as nearly as circumstances admit. The notice specifies the number offered and a time not less than fifteen days or such lesser number of days as may be prescribed and not exceeding thirty days. Unless the articles otherwise provide, the offer includes a right of renunciation.

sections.heading: Disposition of declined or unaccepted shares
sections.body: After the offer is declined or the time expires, the Board may dispose of the shares in a manner not disadvantageous to the shareholders and the company.

sections.heading: Notice dispatch
sections.body: The rights-offer notice shall be despatched through registered post, speed post or electronic mode to all existing shareholders at least three days before the opening of the issue.

sections.heading: Employee stock option route
sections.body: Further shares may be offered to employees under an employees’ stock option scheme subject to special resolution and prescribed conditions.

sections.heading: Preferential issue
sections.body: Further shares may be offered to any persons if authorised by special resolution, for cash or other consideration, if the price is determined by the valuation report of a registered valuer, subject to Chapter III and prescribed conditions.

sections.heading: Conversion and Government-directed issue
sections.body: Section 62 provides for conversion of loans or debentures into shares where the conversion terms were approved by special resolution before issue, and for Government-directed conversion under sub-sections (4)–(6).

examples.title: Rights offer
examples.body: The company sends a letter of offer to equity holders pro rata, with a 21-day acceptance window and renunciation right, despatched at least three days before opening. Section 62(1)(a) and (2) are followed.

examples.title: Preferential issue
examples.body: By special resolution and with a registered-valuer report, the company issues further shares to a strategic investor. Section 62(1)(c) is used; section 42 may also apply.

hypotheticals.question: A company wants to allot further shares to a strategic investor rather than first offering them pro rata to existing equity holders. What route must be analysed?
hypotheticals.analysis: The default is a rights offer under section 62(1)(a). An issue to other persons requires the special resolution and prescribed conditions under section 62(1)(c), including registered-valuer pricing; section 42 private-placement requirements may also apply.

hypotheticals.question: A company wants to use a shorter rights-offer period. Can it simply set a shorter deadline?
hypotheticals.analysis: The Act allows a time not less than fifteen days or such lesser number of days as may be prescribed, and not exceeding thirty days. Any shorter period must rest on the current prescribed rule and its exact conditions (including private-company consent conditions where applicable).

distinctions.title: Further issue (s. 62) vs private placement (s. 42)
distinctions.left: Section 62 governs rights, ESOP and preferential further-issue routes
distinctions.right: Section 42 governs the separate private-placement procedure

rows.left: Shareholder pre-emption and permitted further-issue routes
rows.right: Offer/invitation to identified persons and private-placement compliance

misconceptions.trap: The Board can always issue further shares to any person without shareholder approval.
misconceptions.correction: The default is a pro-rata rights offer; ESOP and preferential routes require special resolution and prescribed conditions.

misconceptions.trap: Renunciation is always excluded or always unconditional.
misconceptions.correction: Unless the articles otherwise provide, the rights offer includes renunciation; apply the articles and applicable rules.

misconceptions.trap: Section 62 preferential issue and section 42 private placement are interchangeable.
misconceptions.correction: Apply the separate requirements of each provision where the transaction engages them.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 62 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the proposed further issue. II. Classify the route (rights / ESOP / preferential / conversion). III. Apply the statutory conditions for that route (period, renunciation, special resolution, valuation, notice dispatch). IV. Check whether section 42 or section 23 also applies. V. Conclude.

bareActPointers: Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, as amended
examTips: Identify the route: rights, ESOP, preferential, conversion or Government-directed issue.
For rights issues: pro-rata, offer period (15 days or lesser prescribed–30 days), renunciation, 3-day dispatch, Board disposal.
For ESOP/preferential: special resolution and current rule/valuation conditions.
Check whether section 42 and section 23 also apply.
revisionPoints: Rights offer is the default under section 62(1)(a)
Offer period: not less than 15 days or lesser prescribed, not exceeding 30 days
Notice despatch at least 3 days before opening
ESOP and preferential require special resolution
Conversion and Government-directed routes under sub-ss (3)–(6)
